definition.description: From a declared walking-to-submaximal start, take one purposeful step into a marked stop zone, lower the center of mass as the foot contacts, absorb into a controlled split or athletic stop position, hold for the declared duration without an extra recovery step, then reset. One repetition contains one planned step-in, one braking contact, and one terminal stick; it is not a box step-down, jog-to-stop, cut, or reacceleration.

environment.surface: clean dry level high-traction non-slip floor or lane
environment.space: one marked step-in and finish station with clear entry and exit
inspection: surface, footwear, marker visibility, clearance, and stop signal
coach sightline to foot contact, knee, hip, trunk, and terminal hold
environment.changeRule: Changing direction, lead side, entry speed, support, finish, hold, surface, cue, dose, symptoms, or substitute requires revalidation.

selectionPrerequisites: pain-free walking and controlled split/athletic stance
can follow a one-step stop, terminal hold, and stop signal
safe station and session braking, lower-body, technical-fatigue, logistics, and duration budgets fit
excludeOrEscalate: pain, giving way, slip, unsafe surface, line miss, foot slide, collapse, unplanned recovery step, imbalance, or communication conflict
new neurologic, circulation, breathing, chest, balance, or coordination concern
notEstablishedByEvidence: universal direction, entry speed, hold, dose, recovery, readiness threshold, clinical clearance, or outcome

provenance.identityAuthority: Landing/braking progressions packet: the stable identity is a low-speed one-step horizontal brake into a terminal stick. Direction is delivery-specific; support and jogging change variants, while a box step-down is a separate vertical strength/control task.

anatomy.laterality: record lead/braking side and direction; program both sides when the delivery context requires it, without assigning athlete skill labels
anatomy.claimsBoundary: Describes task mechanics and plausible loading sites only; it does not diagnose, treat, prevent injury, establish readiness, or guarantee transfer.

athleteSupport.whyItMatters: Candidate practice for one controlled low-speed braking contact and terminal stance only when the exact direction, marker, surface, and session budget fit.
athleteSupport.primaryCue: Step to the marker, lower into the stop, and freeze without another step.
secondaryCues: put pressure through the whole foot
let ankle, knee, and hip share the braking
keep the knee tracking over the middle toes
expectedSensations: light-to-moderate front-thigh, hip, calf, foot, and trunk braking effort
attention to one clean step and terminal balance
unexpectedSensations: pain, giving way, slip, foot slide, knee/trunk collapse, dizziness, or inability to hold
athleteSupport.painGuidance: Stop rather than forcing a step, range, or hold through pain, instability, dizziness, or another concerning symptom; report it and follow facility escalation policy.
selfChecks: one planned step reached the marker
the contact lowered into the stop rather than reached stiffly
the terminal position held without a recovery step
no box, jogging approach, cut, or reacceleration was added

observationChecklist: exact entry direction, lead side, marker, no-box/no-running boundary, surface, and hold
foot placement, whole-foot pressure, knee/trunk control, terminal balance, and side asymmetry
valid repetitions, first fault, symptoms, rest, and downstream braking exposure

faultCorrections.reaching_or_slide: shorten the step and restore whole-foot controlled contact
faultCorrections.upright_stiff_contact: slow the entry and restore ankle-knee-hip lowering
faultCorrections.collapse: reduce demand only if alignment returns; otherwise stop and revalidate another reviewed task
faultCorrections.recovery_step: reduce entry speed and restore the terminal hold before counting repetitions

demonstrationPlan: show marker, one purposeful step, lowering, terminal hold, reset, and stop signal
show valid whole-foot contact and no recovery step
show invalid box step-down, jog entry, stiff reach, collapse, and extra step
confirm the athlete can state the marker, hold, and stop signal
groupManagement: use one visible station per athlete with clear entry/exit
stagger starts so foot contact and terminal hold remain observable
record lead side, direction, valid repetitions, first fault, symptoms, rest, and braking exposure
modificationDecisionTree: if pain, giving way, slip, dizziness, unsafe floor, or communication failure occurs, stop and escalate under facility policy
if one-step control cannot be restored, shorten or slow the entry only if quality returns
if support, jogging, cut, reacceleration, or box height is required, select a separately reviewed exact task and rerun validation
do not automatically substitute a box step-down or jog-to-stick
doNotUseWhen: the intended task is box step-down strength, running deceleration, cut/reacceleration, assessment, or conditioning
surface, symptoms, terminal control, supervision, or communication is inadequate

supportOperations.supportEscalation: Stop and escalate unresolved symptoms, unsafe setup, repeated slide/collapse/recovery steps, or a mismatch between the requested task and this exact single-step brake-to-stick contract.
supportOperations.retentionPolicy: Persist versioned definition and exact variant, direction, lead side, valid repetitions, first fault, terminal hold, symptoms, rest, substitution, stop reason, and generator/rendering versions under facility policy.
supportOperations.changeImpactPolicy: Any change to direction, lead side, entry speed, support, finish, hold, surface, cue, dose, or substitute reruns selection, fatigue, impact, logistics, duration, substitutions, and validation.

sourceVariant.displayName: Step-In to Stick Legacy Skeleton — Source 223
sourceVariant.archiveReason: The source lacks exact direction, lead side, entry, terminal hold, load, fatigue, delivery, alternate, support, and review contracts.

legacy.description: Take one controlled step into the marker, lower into a stable stop, hold, then reset.
legacy.tempo: one planned step; lower through contact; two-second terminal stick; reset
legacy.loadNote: Low bodyweight horizontal braking. Exact direction, lead side, entry, hold, rest, and lower-body overlap are delivery-profile specific.
legacy.cardSummary: Candidate one-step horizontal deceleration card with explicit no-box, no-running, terminal-hold, and stop boundaries.
legacy.coachLanguage: Count only one-step controlled stops that own the terminal position.
legacy.athleteLanguage: Step to the marker, lower into the stop, freeze, reset, and report symptoms.

safety.prerequisiteNotes: Readiness is the exact single step, direction, terminal stance, surface, symptom, supervision, and fatigue context—not a participant classification.
readinessChecks: pain-free walking and controlled split/athletic stance
one controlled stop without a recovery step
clear dry high-traction station and known stop signal
session braking and technical-fatigue budgets fit
stopSigns: pain, giving way, slip, foot slide, line miss, repeated collapse, unplanned recovery step, unsafe station, or participant stop request
inability to restore a controlled one-step terminal hold after rest
contraindications: symptom, unsafe surface, inadequate one-step braking control, supervision, or communication
box step-down, jogging entry, cut, reacceleration, or testing intent without a separately reviewed contract
commonSubstitutions: Use another reviewed task only after full revalidation.
Do not automatically substitute a box step-down or jog-to-stick.

score.difficultyRationale: The score describes task complexity and physical difficulty for one low-speed horizontal step-in brake-to-stick only, not participant ability, experience, age, or readiness. One-step timing, posture, force attenuation, and terminal control exceed its low physical demand.

difficultyProfile.notes: Exact one-step horizontal braking contact and terminal hold; no box, running, cut, or reacceleration.

variants.displayName: Low-Speed Single-Step Horizontal Deceleration to Terminal Stick

programmingProfile.weeklyExposure: candidate_review_required; program from current braking exposure rather than a universal frequency
programmingProfile.completionCriteria: each repetition uses one planned braking step, reaches the marker, owns the terminal hold, and has no stop event
programmingProfile.sequenceRules: Place before jog-to-stick or higher-momentum braking when one-step position and force-attenuation quality are the priority.
programmingProfile.pairingCompatibility: May pair with mobility, trunk control, or noncompeting upper-body work when station, recovery, and total lower-body exposure remain valid.
programmingProfile.interferenceRules: Do not stack with high-speed deceleration, cutting, high-impact jumps, exhaustive lower-body work, or testing when terminal quality degrades.
programmingProfile.uncertaintyPolicy: Scores, dose, recovery, and progression are candidate planning estimates; require human review and rerun validation after any change.

deliveryProfiles.purpose: Rehearse one controlled low-speed braking contact and terminal stance without running momentum.
deliveryProfiles.qualityGate: One planned step reaches the marker, lowers under control, holds without recovery step, and has no stop event.
stopRules: pain, instability, slip, unsafe station, or participant request
slide, collapse, line miss, recovery step, or inability to hold
deliveryProfiles.coachInstructions: Declare side, direction, marker, and hold. Observe the contact and count only controlled terminal stops.
deliveryProfiles.athleteInstructions: Step to the marker, lower as the foot lands, freeze without another step, then reset.
deliveryProfiles.expectedAdaptation: Task-specific one-step horizontal braking rehearsal; no universal outcome is claimed.

logistics.durationFormula: setup plus valid repetitions, rest, restarts, recording, and reset

doseScaling.entry: slow the step before adding repetitions
doseScaling.volume: add only while every terminal hold remains controlled

supportPrompts.coach: Control the stop; do not turn it into a run.
